issues.t: Timing chain stretch and VVT rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A loud ticking or rattling for a few seconds right after a cold start, or a knocking or rattle from the front of the engine at low engine speeds once it is warm. The check engine light may come on.
issues.why: The variable valve timing (VVT) actuator on the cam gear wears at its locking pin, and the timing chain can stretch. Mazda admitted the problem and extended coverage on the repair to 7 years or 70,000 miles for most 2007-2010 turbo CX-7s; that extension has now run out.
issues.next: Do not ignore a cold-start rattle. Have a shop check the timing chain and VVT actuator soon, and keep up with oil changes using 5W-30. Catching it early is far cheaper than repairing an engine after the chain jumps.

issues.t: Engine destroyed when the timing chain or VVT gear breaks
issues.sym: The engine suddenly dies while driving and will crank but not start, sometimes after weeks of ticking or rattling noises.
issues.why: If a worn VVT actuator breaks or a stretched timing chain jumps or snaps, the pistons hit the valves. This turbo engine has no room for error there, so the damage is usually severe.
issues.next: Have it towed rather than trying to restart it over and over. A shop can check compression to see how much damage there is; often a replacement engine is the most sensible fix.

issues.sym: A loud whine or siren noise when accelerating, weak acceleration, blue or gray smoke from the exhaust, and a check engine light.
issues.why: The turbo spins very fast and relies on a steady supply of clean oil. Oil sludge, a clogged oil feed or return line, and long gaps between oil changes wear out its bearings and seals. Owners often report failures well before 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Stop hard driving and have the turbo and its oil lines checked. When the turbo is replaced, the oil feed line and screen should be cleaned or replaced too, or the new turbo can fail the same way.

issues.t: Blue or white exhaust smoke from turbo oil seepage
issues.sym: Puffs of blue or white smoke from the tailpipe, especially after idling or on startup, and oil level dropping between changes.
issues.why: Pressure in the crankcase ventilation system can push oil past the turbo seals. Mazda issued service bulletins and a special service program for oil leaking past the turbo seal on this engine.
issues.next: Check the oil level often so the engine never runs low. Ask a Mazda dealer to check your VIN for any bulletin work and have the PCV system and turbo seals inspected.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power while driving
issues.sym: The SUV suddenly loses power or goes into a reduced-power limp mode while driving, sometimes with the check engine light flashing or on.
issues.why: Owners tie this to turbo boost problems, failing VVT parts and throttle body faults on the turbo engine. Mazda bulletins also cover lack of power from intake and fuel mixture sensor faults.
issues.next: If power drops, move to a safe spot and have the trouble codes read. Do not keep driving with a flashing check engine light.

issues.t: A/C compressor clutch fails and A/C blows warm
issues.sym: The air conditioning suddenly blows warm air. In some cases the compressor clutch seizes, causing a burning smell, smoke from under the hood or a squealing drive belt.
issues.why: The A/C compressor and its magnetic clutch fail early on many of these SUVs. Mazda extended A/C coverage to 60,000 miles, but many owners report failures shortly after that.
issues.next: If you smell burning or see smoke when the A/C is on, turn it off and have it checked; a seized clutch can damage the drive belt. A shop can tell you whether the clutch alone or the whole compressor needs replacing.

issues.t: Front ball joints can corrode and separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end over bumps, loose or wandering steering, or in the worst case a front wheel that suddenly tilts or loses control.
issues.why: Water can get into the front lower ball joints. In areas that use road salt the joints corrode, and the ball joint can pull out of the lower control arm. Mazda recalled all 2007-2012 CX-7s and replaces both front lower control arms for free.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or with a Mazda dealer and get the free control arm replacement if it has not been done. If you hear front-end clunks, have it inspected before driving far.

issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. The danger is that in a crash the passenger airbag inflator can burst and throw metal fragments.
issues.why: The Takata passenger airbag inflators used in these SUVs can break down after years of heat and humidity. Mazda recalled every 2007-2012 CX-7 in a series of recalls, and some cars need a second replacement.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls right away. The replacement is free at any Mazda dealer, and it matters even if a replacement was done years ago.

issues.t: Low-beam headlights burn out or fail from moisture
issues.sym: Low-beam bulbs burn out again and again, one headlight works only now and then, or you see fog and water droplets inside the headlight or tail light.
issues.why: Moisture can get inside the lamp housings, and Mazda issued bulletins for headlight condensation and for low beams that stop working because of moisture. Owners of 2010 models report frequent bulb failures.
issues.next: Check your headlights often, since a dark headlight is a ticket and a safety risk. Ask a dealer about the moisture bulletins; drying and resealing the housing, or replacing it, can stop the repeat failures.

issues.t: Rough idle and lack of power with lean fuel codes
issues.sym: Rough idle, weak acceleration and a check engine light with codes P2177 or P2187 (engine running too lean).
issues.why: Mazda bulletins trace this to the air-fuel sensor wiring and engine software on early turbo CX-7s, which can make the engine run lean.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask a dealer to check for software updates and the related bulletins before replacing sensors.

issues.t: Unstable idle or stalling from a dirty throttle body
issues.sym: Idle speed hunts up and down, the engine stumbles or stalls when coming to a stop, and in some cases a check engine light with limp-home mode.
issues.why: Carbon builds up in the electronic throttle body, which upsets idle control. Mazda issued bulletins for unstable idle and stalling from throttle body deposits and for a throttle fault code that can trigger limp mode.
issues.next: Have a shop clean the throttle body and relearn the idle. If limp mode codes come back, the throttle body may need to be replaced.

issues.t: Check engine light from a stuck intake shutter valve
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P2006.
issues.why: The intake shutter valve that changes air flow at low speed can stick closed. Mazda handled it with a service bulletin and an emissions recall.
issues.next: Have a Mazda dealer check your VIN for the emissions campaign; the fix may be free.

issues.t: Check engine light from an evap leak at the fuel filler pipe
issues.sym: Check engine light with an evaporative leak code such as P0455, often with no drivability problem.
issues.why: The fuel filler pipe may not seal well, letting fuel vapor escape. Mazda issued bulletins for evap leak codes on these SUVs.
issues.next: First make sure the gas cap is tight and in good shape. If the light returns, have a smoke test done on the evap system.

issues.t: Squeak from the front stabilizer bar
issues.sym: A squeak or creak from the front suspension when driving over rough roads or speed bumps.
issues.why: The front stabilizer bar bushings can dry out and squeak. Mazda issued a bulletin for this on 2007-2009 CX-7s.
issues.next: Not a safety issue. A shop can replace the bushings with the updated parts.

issues.t: Clunk from a worn engine mount
issues.sym: A clunk from the engine bay over rough roads or when shifting between drive and reverse.
issues.why: One of the engine mounts can wear and let the engine move too much. Mazda issued a bulletin for a clunk over rough roads traced to the No. 3 engine mount.
issues.next: Have the mounts checked. A failing mount is not urgent but can stress hoses and the exhaust if ignored.

issues.t: Gear oil leak from the transfer case seal
issues.sym: Gear oil drips or wetness near the transfer case behind the engine on all-wheel-drive models, and sometimes a burning smell.
issues.why: A transfer case seal on early all-wheel-drive CX-7s can leak. Mazda issued a bulletin for gear oil dripping from this seal.
issues.next: Check for drips and have the transfer case fluid level checked. Running it low can ruin the transfer case, which is expensive.

issues.t: Airbag warning light from a wiring fault
issues.sym: The airbag (SRS) warning light stays on.
issues.why: Mazda issued bulletins for airbag warning lights on these SUVs caused by high resistance in airbag circuits and connector faults.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read soon. While the light is on, the airbags may not work in a crash.

issues.sym: Squealing brakes, a pulsing pedal or steering wheel shake when braking, or brakes that feel like they are dragging.
issues.why: Mazda issued several bulletins for brake noise, judder and drag on the CX-7, often from rotor wear and sticking pads or calipers.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected. Resurfacing or replacing the rotors and servicing the calipers usually fixes it.

issues.t: Musty smell from the A/C vents
issues.sym: A musty or mildew smell when the A/C or fan first turns on.
issues.why: Moisture on the A/C evaporator lets mold grow. Mazda issued bulletins on this odor.
issues.next: Replace the cabin air filter and have the evaporator cleaned. Running the fan with the A/C off for a few minutes before parking helps.
